title: memory-safety-recall-workflow-128k-surge
content:
Summary:
This note captures a focused eval run and regression investigation for memory-safety / recall under heavy retrieval and very-long-context scenarios (8k, 32k, 128k). The aim was to reproduce intermittent attention-sink behavior seen after the last runtime patch (PR 2150) and to map failure modes to KV-cache fragmentation and truncation boundaries introduced by retrieval chaining.

Goals:
- Validate end-to-end recall fidelity across 8k/32k/128k workloads with retrieval-chaining.
- Characterize attention-sink regressions (where model output abruptly degrades mid-generation) and their correlation with retrieval insertion points.
- Produce a prioritized mitigation plan for onboarding new model variants that will be served on Dedicated and Private.

High-level findings (TL;DR):
- Reproducible attention-sink events at 32k+ when retrieval chunks are inserted at token offsets that align with KV-cache segment boundaries (observed approx every ~32k tokens in our segmented encoder flow).
- 128k runs show two failure classes: (A) short-term recall drop when large retrievals push earlier prefix blinding (partial truncation of prefix in KV), (B) catastrophic attention collapse when many small retrievals fragment the KV cache and trigger kernel-path fallback with a different attention implementation.
- Throughput/latency tradeoffs: aggressive prefetching reduces probability of sink but increases 95p latency by ~12% on Ampere A100 80GB.

Test matrix (executed):
- Models: onboarding-13B-q4 (fp16 + custom quant), onboarding-70B-fp16, baseline-open-70b-v1 (control)
- Workloads: conversational-retrieval (document chunks sized 512/2048/8192 tokens), summarization-of-chain (long chaining with 10–60 retrievals per request), synthetic attention-stress (repeated prefix replay to force KV reuse)
- Context sizes exercised: 8k, 32k, 128k (simulated by concatenating retrieval results + conversation history)
- Routes: local-dedicated (no network variability), hosted-simulated (adds 10–40ms jitter)
- Metrics collected: token-level perplexity drift, recall@k for ground-truth spans, generation-length-to-failure (tokens generated before first incoherent token), p(UNK)/repetition rate, latency p50/p95, kernel-path id logs

Prompt sets / canonical cases included (examples):
- Retrieval-chain QA (short answer):
  Prompt: "User: Given the documents provided, what technique did the 2005 paper propose to reduce network churn? Answer succinctly."
  Retrieval: chain length 12 (each chunk ~1024 tokens), inserted one-per-1000 tokens.

- Longform synthesis (multi-doc):
  Prompt: "Summarize the combined policy changes across the dataset and highlight contradictions."
  Retrieval: 48 docs, mixed sizes, targeted overlapping sections to stress attention overlap.

- Attention sink stress probe (synthetic):
  Prompt: repeated visibility of the same long prefix repeated 8x across the context to force KV reuse/overlap; then a small retrieval inserted right at generation offset 32768.

Observed regression patterns (detailed):
1) Truncation-induced anchor loss:
   - When retrieval insertions cause the effective prefix to be truncated (KV windows drop earliest tokens), model loses anchor tokens used to ground factual answers; recall@5 drops 18–32% at 128k vs 32k.
   - Symptoms: confident but incorrect short answers referencing hallucinated entities.

2) Fragmented KV cache -> mixed kernel execution:
   - Small frequent retrievals (<=512 tokens) result in fragmented KV pages. The runtime elects an optimized kernel for dense contiguous KV and falls back to a compatibility kernel for fragmented cases; fallback kernel exhibits different attention normalization causing token collapse in some seeds.
   - Deterministic repro when fragment count > 60 within a single request.

3) Attention saturation near segment boundaries:
   - Generations that cross internal per-layer attention window boundaries show a spike in p(UNK) and local repetition. This maps to the known internal checkpointing that happens at ~32k multiples.

Quantitative snapshot (select numbers):
- Recall@5 (baseline-open-70b-v1): 0.78 (32k), 0.72 (128k)
- Recall@5 (onboarding-70B-fp16): 0.75 (32k), 0.56 (128k, high fragmentation)
- Mean tokens-to-failure (attention sink): onboarding-13B-q4 = 14k tokens median at 128k workload, baseline-open = 48k tokens median
- Latency p95 change with prefetch: +12% on A100 80GB, but attention-sink probability drops from 0.18 -> 0.05 per-request in the 128k synth workload

Qualitative failure excerpts (real logs sanitized):
- Case A (truncation anchor loss): "...the policy is implemented by the Board of Transit. The Board of Transit was established in 1989 and abolished in 1812." (temporal contradiction)
- Case B (kernel-fallback sink): "...the experiment shows zero. zero. zero. zero. zero." repeated until cutoff

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV fragmentation causes kernel path switch which changes numerical stability of softmax across layers -> leads to token collapse in rare seeds.
2) Truncation policy in router incorrectly computes prefix eviction points when retrievals are appended vs prefetched, producing dropped grounding tokens.
3) Combined effect of quantization noise (q4) and fragmented caching amplifies attention drift at 128k-scale.

Mitigations attempted in-run (and results):
- Aggressive prefetch (append retrievals into a single contiguous KV region before serving): reduced fragmentation events by ~65% and sink prob by ~72% but increased p95 latency.
- Soft fallback threshold tuning: raise fallback kernel threshold to prefer optimized kernel unless fragmentation severe -> reduced sinks but left some incorrect recalls due to truncated anchors.
- Prompt anchoring: add synthetic anchor token sequence at regular intervals to keep grounding tokens in KV; helped recall in ~40% of failing cases but is a brittle app-level hack.

Recommended onboarding checklist for new model variants (practical):
- Run the full test matrix with both append and prefetch retrieval modes. Record kernel-path histograms and fragmentation counts.
- Add deterministic seeds for attention-sink probe (we used seeds [103, 209, 401]) and ensure 0 false positives in acceptance for Dedicated tier onboarding.
- If quantized variant (q4/q5) is used, run extended 128k batch for 48 hours to capture rare seeds.
- Include a KV-fragmentation-aware rollout: start with low retrieval density (<=12 retrievals per 128k) and progressively increase while monitoring tokens-to-failure.

Operational playbook sketch (short-term):
- On detecting attention-sink in production, auto-route to fallback model variant with forced prefetch and increased latency budget. Emit alert tagging fragmentation_count, kernel_path, and recent retrieval insertion offsets.
- Dashboard additions: new metric 'kv_fragmentation_count' and 'kernel_path_ratio' per-request. Add a gating alert when fragmentation_count > 40 & sink probability > 0.1.

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- Does a per-layer softmax-temperature tweak (software shim) in fallback kernel reduce collapse without sacrificing quality? (exp planned: kernel-temp sweep)
- Can we reduce fragmentation by changing retrieval chunking policy (prefer 2048-sized chunks) and is that better for recall distribution?
- How much of the failure rate is due to quantization vs kernel path numeric stability? need ablation with fp16 pure runs on same hardware.

Action items (owners):
- Ethan K: reproduce fragmentation->kernel-switch with a micro-benchmark that reports the exact layer where softmax instability shows (due 2025-02-20).
- Priya N: implement kv_fragmentation_count telemetry in serving runtime and add to per-request trace (due 2025-02-28).
- Sofia L: run full onboarding regression for onboarding-70B-fp16 with prefetch/apppend toggles and produce a pass/fail matrix (due 2025-03-05).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is a working investigation (not final). Data attached in linked PRs and JIRA. If you want reproducer scripts, see PR 2150 / test harness branch '128k-kv-frag-repro'.
- For immediate demos to sales, use the prefetch config as a conservative default for Dedicated customers until kernel numeric fixes land.

Unresolved / known gaps:
- We still see non-deterministic seeds that only fail on specific hardware generations (Ampere vs Hopper) — requires hardware matrix testing.
- We need better synthetic prompt suites that stress overlapping retrieval semantics (I propose a small corpus 'overlap-24k' to be created).

-- end --
